newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's ACOSS sees overrun on welfare deficits.
newsitem.headline: France's ACOSS sees overrun on welfare deficits.

text.p: France's ACOSS, the central agency for social security, said on Tuesday it estimated the French welfare deficit would reach 54.2 billion francs in 1996 and 35.2 bilion in 1997, both slightly higher than expected.
The Social Security Accounts Commission had estimated the welfare deficit for 1996 at 51.5 billion, while the government had forecast for 1997 a deficit of 30.4 billion.
The government is committed to curbing welfare spending in order to meet its target of reducing the total public deficit to three percent of GDP this year to qualify for European monetary union.
The welfare figures were given by an ACOSS official who had been asked to comment on a report on welfare deficits in business daily Les Echos.
He said the overrun in 1996 was partly due to a regularisation of payments to hospitals in 1996.
In 1997, the overrun was due to a slower-than-expected rise in national wages, on which funding is based, of 2.7 percent instead of 3.3 percent initially expected.
The social security system, which funds pensions, healthcare and family benefits, is financed mainly through payroll taxes and has been hit badly in recent years by the rise in unemployment.
The official said deficit figures due to be established by the Social Security Accounts Commission could be slightly different from those estimated by ACOSS.
ACOSS estimates have however been very accurate in previous years.
